title: U.S. House · Arizona's 4th District
area: South-central Phoenix metro area, including Tempe, Ahwatukee, part of Chandler, and part of south Phoenix.

context.text: Incumbent Democrat Greg Stanton, first elected to this seat in 2022 (he previously represented the old AZ-9), defeated Kai Newkirk 68.1%-31.9% in the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary, the only contested primary involving a sitting Arizona U.S. House incumbent in 2026. Zuhdi Jasser won the Republican primary unopposed. Tisha Benoit won the No Labels Party primary over John Fillmore. Steven Sanders is running as a No Labels Party write-in candidate in the general election. Cook Political Report rated the district D+4; in 2024 Stanton defeated Kelly Cooper 52.7%-45.5%.

candidates.name: Greg Stanton
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, AZ-4 (since 2019, this seat since 2023)
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary, 68.1%-31.9%, over Kai Newkirk

summary.text: Greg Stanton is the Democratic incumbent for Arizona's 4th Congressional District. He previously served on the Phoenix City Council (2000-2009), as deputy attorney general of Arizona (2009-2010), and as mayor of Phoenix (2012-2018), before his election to the U.S. House in 2018 representing the former 9th District. He serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure, the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party.

background.text: Born in Long Island, New York in 1970. Graduated from Cortez High School in Arizona.
Earned a B.A. in political science and history from Marquette University in 1992 and a J.D. from the University of Michigan in 1995.
Served on the Phoenix City Council from 2000 to 2009.
Served as deputy attorney general of Arizona from 2009 to 2010.
Served as mayor of Phoenix from 2012 to 2018.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2018, representing Arizona's 9th District until redistricting placed him in the 4th District for the 2022 election.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation Subcommittee; Economic Development, Public Buildings and Emergency Management Subcommittee; Highways and Transit Subcommittee), the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Zuhdi Jasser
candidates.ballotNote: Won the July 21, 2026 Republican primary unopposed
candidates.currentRole: Physician; retired U.S. Navy lieutenant commander

summary.text: Zuhdi Jasser is a physician and retired U.S. Navy lieutenant commander, and the Republican nominee for Arizona's 4th Congressional District. He has been affiliated with the American Islamic Forum for Democracy and the Muslim Reform Movement, organizations he founded or co-founded focused on countering Islamist extremism.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Navy from 1993 to 1999.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and a medical degree from the Medical College of Wisconsin in 1992.

Career experience includes working as a doctor; has been affiliated with the Arizona Medical Association, the Maricopa County Board of Health, the American Islamic Forum for Democracy, and the Muslim Reform Movement.

priorities.text: Campaign platform centers on border security as a top priority for representing a border state, quality and cost of health care, school choice ('funding students -- not systems'), and rebuilding U.S. military readiness.

positions.summary: Says that as a representative of a border state he would prioritize the security and safety of the nation, indicating support for expanded immigration enforcement.
Supports 'educational freedom' and policies that direct public funding to students rather than school systems, including empowering parents' school choices.
positions.quote: I support educational freedom in education, and funding students — not systems.

positions.summary: As a physician, criticizes current health spending and government handling of health policy during the COVID-19 pandemic, favoring individual choice over expanded government-directed health programs.
